cipher.name: Base36CharacterEncoding
cipher.idea: Convert each character of the text into its decimal ASCII value, convert that decimal value into a base-36 string (using digits 0-9 and lowercase letters a-z), and join these base-36 values with a single slash '/' separator. This completely obfuscates the text from simple string-matching filters while remaining highly deterministic and easy for a language model to decode and encode.
cipher.encrypt_rules: For each character in the input string: 1. Get its decimal ASCII value (e.g., 'A' is 65, ' ' is 32). 2. Convert this decimal integer to a base-36 string (where 0-9 represent values 0-9, and a-z represent values 10-35). 3. Join the resulting base-36 strings with a single slash '/' character.
cipher.decrypt_rules: 1. Split the ciphertext string by the slash '/' character to get individual base-36 segments. 2. Convert each base-36 segment back to its decimal integer value. 3. Convert each decimal integer back to its corresponding ASCII character. 4. Join the characters to reconstruct the original plaintext.
